status: frozen before any comparative run; the plugin list, sources, mechanisms, effects and rule may not change after an outcome is seen
scope: Unmodified popular Bash plugins loaded through each framework's documented mechanism in a private fixture, with GNU Readline as the editor for every framework. Separate from release evidence.

environment.bash: the image's /bin/bash; its version and SHA-256 are recorded with every result
environment.private_home: a new HOME per framework and per shell, with INPUTRC=/dev/null, HISTFILE inside that HOME, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, TERM=xterm-256color, no inherited BASH_ENV, ENV or BASH_FUNC_ variables
environment.pty: scripts/terminal.py Terminal, an interactive login-free shell reading only the private ~/.bashrc
environment.network: none while shells run; sources are staged and hashed before the run

binit.source: the Binit source under test, built in the image; its commit is recorded
binit.startup: eval "$(binit init)" followed by one binit plugin line per plugin, then binit sync in a setup shell

bash-it.startup: a clone of the pinned revision copied to ~/.bash_it, then install.sh --silent, which writes the template ~/.bashrc and enables the default profile

oh-my-bash.startup: tools/install.sh --unattended with OSH_REPOSITORY set to a clone of the pinned revision, which writes the template ~/.bashrc; its plugins and completions arrays are edited only to add the plugin under test

git-completion.source: the distribution's /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/git from the snapshot's git package
git-completion.effect: Completing `git ch` with the registered completion (loading it through a default completion loader first when one is registered) offers both checkout and cherry-pick.

bash-completion.source: the distribution's /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion from the snapshot's bash-completion package
bash-completion.effect: BASH_COMPLETION_VERSINFO is at least 2, _comp_initialize or _init_completion exists, a default completion loader is registered, and calling it for make registers make's completion.

fzf.install: the binary in /usr/local/bin and the tag's shell/ directory in /opt/fzf/shell

mechanisms.bash-it: ~/.fzf.bash containing eval "$(fzf --bash)", as fzf's installer writes it, then bash-it enable plugin fzf

fzf.effect: fzf-file-widget and __fzf_history__ exist, bind -X lists both as key commands, and `printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' | fzf --filter beta` prints beta.

nvm.install: nvm.sh alone in a private NVM_DIR=$HOME/.nvm, as nvm's manual install describes; no Node is installed

mechanisms.binit: binit plugin $HOME/.nvm id=nvm files=nvm.sh load=command commands=nvm

nvm.effect: nvm --version prints the compared version and NVM_DIR holds no installed Node afterwards.

editor_pairings.not_covered: ble.sh with any framework; Binit's native menu on or off is recorded but not compared

rule: Per plugin, a framework passes when every assertion of the plugin's effect holds in a fresh shell. Win: Binit passes strictly more plugins and every plugin another framework passes. Tie: the same passing set. Loss: another framework passes a plugin Binit fails. Anything else is inconclusive. A plugin unsupported by a framework's documented mechanism is a failure for that framework, reported as unsupported.

steps: Start from nvm 0.40.2 declared from its own private directory and record the selected generation.
Pinned update: declare nvm 0.40.3 instead, sync, and check a fresh shell reports 0.40.3 on a new generation.
Failed update: declare a source whose file is missing, sync, and check the sync fails and the selected generation is unchanged.
Rollback: binit rollback, and check the selected generation is exactly the first one and a fresh shell reports 0.40.2.
Fresh shell: every plugin effect still holds on the rolled-back generation.
binit_lifecycle.user_definition: A user function defined in ~/.bashrc after the plugin lines exists in the live shell after each sync and in every fresh shell.
